RQ1.rationale: Central contribution is a reusable CubeSat System Reference Model for mission-specific CubeSat systems.

RQ2.rationale: Discusses reuse, reproducibility/access, interoperability, and traceability outcomes at system level, but not EPS-derived reliability/reproducibility/integrability evidence.

RQ3.rationale: Contains integrated system-level V&V activity elements and trace relationships, but not EPS-specific pre-physical verification procedures.

bibliographic_review_management.lineage_overlap_notes: Part of the INCOSE SSWG CSRM lineage; cites Interim Status #4 and related 2017/2018 papers on CubeSat behaviors and technical measurement. Treat as recurring reference-model lineage rather than independent mission evidence.

study_context_population.mission_platform: Generic CubeSat/nanosatellite-class space and ground system reference model; no named mission case.
study_context_population.size_form_factor: Defines CubeSat 1U as 10x10x10 cm and about 1.3 kg; notes larger 3U, 6U, and 12U form factors.
study_context_population.mission_name: not reported; mission-specific models are hypothetical/for future mission teams
study_context_population.mission_domain: Generic CubeSat missions including space segment, ground segment, launch/deploy interfaces, and regulatory stakeholders; no payload domain is selected.
study_context_population.organization_type: INCOSE Space Systems Working Group develops the CSRM; target users include university-level CubeSat teams; OMG candidate specification path is described.
study_context_population.project_maturity: Reference model implemented in a graphical modeling tool and described as sufficiently mature for validation; mission-team evaluation remains future/prospective.

context_evidence_quotes.quote: The CSRM is intended for use at the university level for designing and building a mission-specific CubeSat.
The CSRM provides the logical architecture of a CubeSat space and ground system.

mbse_objective_scope_artifacts.stated_objective_pain_point: Develop and validate a reusable CubeSat System Reference Model that captures CubeSat space/ground logical architecture and systems-engineering artifacts so university mission teams can tailor it into a mission-specific model and eventual physical architecture.
mbse_objective_scope_artifacts.system_boundary_and_abstraction: Boundary includes CubeSat mission enterprise, space segment, ground segment, CubeSat subsystems/components, ground subsystems/components, stakeholders, regulatory/deployer stakeholders, requirements, technical measures, use cases, and V&V concepts. Abstraction is mainly logical architecture/reference information; physical architecture is created by the mission team from the logical architecture.
mbse_objective_scope_artifacts.minimal_or_excluded_content: CSRM is not pre-populated with mission-specific stakeholders, technical measures, use cases, or requirements; parametrics for power/weight/cost have not been added; physical model details are left to the MSM/mission team.
mbse_objective_scope_artifacts.required_prior_behavioral_domain_knowled: Mission teams must identify their systems-engineering methodology, stakeholders, needs, terminology, relationships, selected artifacts, logical components, physical components, and appropriate requirements truncation/verification strategies. CSRM handles limited prior knowledge by providing a reusable sandbox/reference hierarchy and terms.

evidence_quotes.quote: It is important to note that the structure and content of the CSRM is intended to provide a rich "sand box" of engineering objects and relationships from which a necessary and sufficient, mission-purpose model can be constructed.
The mission team identifies the systems engineering methodology to be followed revising the MSM organization, elements, relationships, and diagrams as required

generality_reuse_mechanism_v1_1_reasonin.rationale: The CSRM is a reusable CubeSat-system reference model/sandbox and logical architecture intended to be instantiated and tailored by mission teams. The paper supports high-level abstraction and mission-agnostic architecture, but not interface-focused model, low-dynamics / non-detailed-behavior model, or specific-mission model with reusable method only.

evidence.quote: The CSRM provides the logical architecture of a CubeSat space and ground system. The CSRM logical components are intended to be reused as a starting point for a mission-specific CubeSat logical architecture

The CSRM is a repository for systems engineering artifacts. However, it is not pre-populated with specific stakeholders, technical measures, use cases, and requirements. That is the job of the mission-specific CubeSat team.
the levels of abstraction in the CSRM for requirements, constraints and logical design are presented as suggestions and must be tailored to the mission purpose.

ivv_integration_level.rationale: The highest supported IVV level is model-contained verification artifacts at generic MSM/system level: Verification/Validation Activity elements, properties, diagrams, tables, and hyperlinks are represented in or linked from the model and are trace-linked to requirements/technical measures. evidence.quote: The Verification Activity element describes the process for verifying an element, e.g. a requirement. The verify relationship is a relationship between a requirement and a test case or other model element that is used to verify the requirement is satisfied.

RQ1: Strongly relevant example of a general CubeSat system-level SysML reference model with reusable logical architecture and systems-engineering artifact structure.
Handles limited mission-specific knowledge by providing a sandbox/reference hierarchy while requiring teams to populate stakeholders, measures, use cases, requirements, and physical architecture.
RQ2: Claims reuse, reproducibility/access, interoperability, traceability, consistency, stakeholder alignment, and lifecycle continuity, but evidence is conceptual and not EPS-specific.
No reliability outcome, EPS outcome, quantitative metric, or baseline comparison is reported.
RQ3: Provides system-level verification and validation activity elements with verify/verified-by and validates/validated-by relationships, test case/procedure links, and active hyperlinks to documents/diagrams.
Does not present an EPS-specific pre-physical verification model, simulation, model checking, SIL/HIL, or hardware integration evidence.

author_stated_limitations_gaps: CSRM is not pre-populated with mission-specific stakeholders, technical measures, use cases, or requirements.
Requirements/constraints/logical design abstraction levels are suggestions and must be tailored to mission purpose.
Validation-requirement satisfaction is initially based on CSRM development-team judgment and should be evaluated by mission-specific CubeSat teams.
Parametrics for power, weight, and cost have not been added because they are more appropriate for a physical model.
CSRM is sufficiently mature for validation and future OMG candidate specification submission, indicating incomplete validation/submission at the interim status.
extractor_identified_limitations_gaps: No EPS-specific outcome evidence despite power subsystem/component references.
No quantitative outcome metrics, baselines, physical test, operational, or flight evidence.
No named modeling tool, model repository URL, or actual XMI/model package is included in the markdown.
Lifecycle continuity through operations is claimed but not demonstrated with downstream operational artifacts or a real mission case.
Part of a recurring CSRM interim-status lineage; avoid double-counting as independent validation evidence.

direct_evidence_quotes.quote: The CSRM provides the logical architecture of a CubeSat space and ground system.
The MSM supports defining requirements development all the way down to the subsystem component level or truncating requirement development based on defining use cases and verification strategies.
The Requirement element has a verified by property.
The CSRM is sufficiently mature for validation to be accomplished followed by submission to OMG for candidate normative specification.

synthesis_consistency.lineage_consistency_notes: Code as the 2019 Interim Status #5 CSRM reference-model paper in the Kaslow/INCOSE SSWG lineage. Reuse/technical-measure/behavior claims overlap with referenced 2017/2018 papers and should not be counted as independent empirical replication unless those papers provide separate evidence.
unexpected_observations: The CSRM includes regulatory and CubeSat deployer stakeholders as model content.
The MSM is proposed as a repository for project-management artifacts, not only engineering artifacts.
Power/weight/cost properties can be rolled up in the physical architecture, but the paper explicitly omits power/weight/cost parametrics at this CSRM stage.
synthesis_consistency.confidence_reason: The paper is clear about reference-model scope, artifacts, and conceptual V&V relationships; main uncertainty concerns the exact venue metadata and the degree of actual model availability/application evidence.

repair_notes: Remove low-dynamics / non-detailed-behavior model from generality_reuse_mechanism unless separately justified; the paper is high-level but does not make nondetailed behavior a reuse mechanism.
Do not add interface-focused model or specific-mission model with reusable method only.
IVV is generic system/MSM-level and model-contained/trace-linked; do not code executable/model-based checks, simulation-in-the-loop, SIL/HIL, or EPS-specific IVV.
Do not code EPS reliability for any claim; C7 should be model consistency/reliability rather than mission assurance.
